notes: Sweep 2026-10-31, five baseline runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2). Each result.json has head 0814e8d, uncommitted false, rc 0, model_id equal to the requested model, files [review.md] and reads []. Every assistant message in each transcript reports only the run's model; each transcript shows a Read of code-review-input.ex and a Write of review.md, no Skill call and no skill file read (no transcript contains the skill's text). Opus-1 also tested its rewrite on SQLite in /tmp/importer-verify; haiku-1 compiled its module with stubs in a check/ folder it left inside its run folder (check/improved.ex equals its review.md block), which result.json's files does not list. Each run's code-review-input.ex equals evals/cases/code-review-input.ex. result.json has no format_ok field, so format_ok comes from this grade's own check.

Rule list: 16 index rows name code-review, the 15 of the 2026-10-23 grade plus the new 'Name a step instead of wrapping an expression' (index cell: not yet graded). git diff d04061d -- idiomatic-elixir/ changes four rules in the list: the new 'Name a step...' rule; the pipeline rule's first bullet, which gains the never-on-one-line, plain-nested-call and mode-argument sentences; 'Match every expected shape...', which gains the `elem/2` sentence and reformats its examples; and the required-keys rule, which gains the `Keyword.fetch!/2` sentence. The `->` rule, renamed 'Inline `->` clauses that read at a glance; otherwise put each body on its own line', and the other rewritten layout rules are outside this case's list and are checked only for other_violations. The 12 unchanged graded rules are graded to the 2026-10-23 standard: a problem counts as reported only when a finding names it or its stated fix addresses it; a silent fix does not count, and a rule is violated when a planted problem belonging to it goes unreported, the improved code keeps it, or the code adds a new instance; a fix of `min(age, 120)` does not report the 120, while a fix naming `@max_age` does; a one-line `if ..., do:` in a `with` body is not nesting; a `_ ->` inside `case Integer.parse(...)` is not counted; `Map.get/2` on a struct breaks the required-keys rule; an assumed or companion changeset counts as a changeset, and hand parsing beside it is allowed; a `change/1,2` that validates nothing breaks the changeset rule.

Deciding sentences for the changed rules. 'Name a step instead of wrapping an expression' (new, no earlier verdict): clean in all five, decided by 'A binding earns its place when it names a recognizable thing or a stage of the computation, holds a value used more than once, ...' and 'It does not when it only renames a value used once (...), when the nested call is plain (...)'. The bindings name a record or stage (haiku-1 line 92 `user = %User{...}`, sonnet-2 line 96 `attrs = %{...}`) or a value used twice (opus-1 line 87 `opts`), and plain nested calls stay nested (opus-1 line 109 `put_change(changeset, :nickname, get_change(changeset, :email))`, haiku-2 line 87 `Repo.insert(struct(User, attrs))`, and every `Mailer.deliver(welcome_email(user))`). 'A line break is not decomposition' is not exercised: no output has an expression that is only wrapped. The one borderline case is sonnet-1 line 55, a 111-character `with` clause holding `insert(%{...})` with an inline map; `mix format` breaks it after `<-` and keeps the call on one line, the formatter's own wrap, so it is not counted. Pipeline rule: decided in all five by the unchanged 'Do not pipe a single step' bullet through the unreported input line 12, and, in three runs, also by the new sentence 'A pipeline never sits on one line, however short: two steps on one line ... hide where one step ends and the next begins, so they go on three lines after `words =`, or become a nested call when there are only two': opus-1 line 89 `params |> import_changeset() |> Repo.insert()`, sonnet-1 line 81 `%User{} |> User.changeset(attrs) |> Repo.insert()` and sonnet-2 line 105 `user |> welcome_email() |> Mailer.deliver()`. The mode-argument sentence ('An argument that only selects a kind or a mode does not start a pipeline') is not exercised; sonnet-1 line 75 `Map.fetch(@roles, role) |> role_result()` starts with a call and breaks the unchanged first and second bullets. 'Match every expected shape...': the new sentence 'The same goes for `elem/2` on a tuple whose shape is known' is not exercised, since no output calls `elem/2`; the verdicts come from the unchanged identical-errors and `_ ->` standard. Required keys: the new sentence 'A keyword list has no dot access: read a key it must hold with `Keyword.fetch!/2`, ..., and keep `opts[:key]` for an option that has a default' keeps every run's option reads (opus-1 `opts[:notify]` after `Keyword.validate!/2` with defaults, the haikus' `opts[:notify]` with a documented `false` default, the sonnets' `Keyword.get(opts, :notify, false)`); haiku-1's violation is decided by the unchanged 'Structs do not implement `Access`: ..., so read struct fields with `user.name` or a pattern', against its line 112 `Map.get(user, :name)`.

Planted problems, mapped as in the 2026-10-23 grades: 21 problems from the case table's 19 rows, with the line 15-17 rebinding counted apart from the magic 120 and the line 49 spawn apart from the closure copy. Counts: opus-1 17, haiku-1 12, haiku-2 11, sonnet-1 15, sonnet-2 16 (2026-10-23: 16; 13, 13; 15, 13). No run reports the line 12 pipe, the line 21 `&&`, the magic 18 or the closure copy. All five report the line 24 lookup-before-insert with the race: opus-1 (finding 5), sonnet-1 (finding 5) and sonnet-2 (finding 5) drop `Repo.get_by/2` for `unique_constraint`; haiku-1 (finding 4) and haiku-2 (finding 6) report it and keep it.

Judgment calls on 'reported'. Opus-1 names no bare-struct insert on its own, but findings 1, 10, 11 and 12 give `cast/3` and `validate_required/2` as the fix and line 5 says the rewrite is built around a changeset, so it counts through its stated fixes (borderline); its magic 120 counts through finding 3's 'Fix: `min(&1, @max_age)`.' Haiku-2's nesting counts through finding 3's 'validate each field explicitly with `with`', and sonnet-1's through finding 3's 'validate with pattern matching and `with`', as 2026-10-23 counted opus-1's `with` fix; haiku-1's finding 3 fix names no `with` and no nesting, so it misses it. Haiku-1's finding 6 ('Bad input, a duplicate, and a failed insert all collapse into `:invalid` or `:insert_failed`') counts for the identical errors but names no dropped changeset, so the line 33 `_ ->` is unreported; haiku-2's finding 3 ('Callers cannot tell bad input from broken code') treats the rescue only as hiding bugs and does not count for the identical errors. Haiku-1's finding 3 ('`params["email"] |> String.downcase()` (line 12) runs before the `is_binary/1` check (line 21)') and sonnet-2's finding 4 count for the dead `is_binary`, not for the pipe or the `&&`. Sonnet-1's finding 10 is about the operators and names no overlap, so its silent drop of `:silent` leaves the overlapping options unreported; sonnet-2's finding 11 ('`opts[:notify] && !opts[:silent]` is redundant; the improved version keeps only `notify`') counts for the overlap. Sonnet-2's finding 11 ('`&&` and `!` should be `and` and `not` for booleans') quotes no line and names `!`, which occurs only on line 27, so it does not count for line 21, as the 2026-10-22-d grade judged a finding of the same shape. Opus-1 reports the overlap (finding 16) and the `Mailer` problem (finding 9) but keeps both by its own statement, which counts them as reported and the 'applies every finding' check as missed.

False positives: sonnet-1 finding 10 rewrites must-not-report line 27's operators, and sonnet-2 finding 11 puts them under `and`/`not` (borderline). Neither puts `and` or `not` on a nil-able option, since both drop `:silent`. Opus-1 treats line 27 only as overlapping options; the haikus do not discuss it. Must-not-report line 11: the why-comment is kept by opus-1 (line 99), sonnet-1 (line 61) and sonnet-2 (line 70); haiku-1 drops it silently and haiku-2 drops it although its finding 9 says it stays. Line 19: opus-1's finding 11 is about blank CSV cells, not the access or `||`, so it is not counted, as before; every run keeps the fallback.

Rules outside the list, checked against their current text for other_violations. Sonnet-1 line 83 is a 106-character `->` clause, which the renamed `->` rule sends to two lines ('a clause whose pattern, `->` and body pass about 70 characters after the indentation goes to two lines'); opus-1's longest clause, line 109, is exactly 70 characters and is not counted. Opus-1's line 89 one-step `with` has a body that cannot fail and no `else`, which the new `with` sentence ('One step is a `with` only when its body cannot fail and there is no `else`') allows. Every `do:` body is one expression on the head's line; no `do:` holds a `fn` or a capture with call arguments; every `fn` passed as an argument holds one call and is on one line where it fits (the `Task.Supervisor.start_child/2` forms would pass 98 characters on one line). No multi-line literal is passed inline after formatting. Directives are in order in every run. The haikus document options under 'Options:' rather than '## Options' and none of them validates options; earlier grades did not list that, so it is not listed.

Format check: the one elixir block in each review.md was extracted to /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-suazi-Repos-idiomatic-elixir-skill/63fbd3f7-5995-424e-b268-7679cfbb08c1/scratchpad/grade-scratch-sweep-2026-10-31/code-review-baseline/baseline-<run>.ex. `mix format --check-formatted` (Elixir 1.20.3) exits 0 for opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2, and fails for sonnet-1 on the line 83 syntax error ('unexpected expression after keyword list', the pattern `[constraint: :unique, _]`). A scratch copy with that pattern written as `[{:constraint, :unique}, _]` (baseline-sonnet-1-patched.ex) still needs formatting at lines 45, 55 and 82-84. A misformatted control (bad.ex) exits 1.

Compile and no-options check: each module was run by drive/run.exs in the scratch folder against real Ecto (Mix.install), an `Accounts.User` schema with email, age, role (`Ecto.Enum` of :admin and :member) and nickname and a `changeset/2` and `import_changeset/2` that cast those fields with `validate_required/2` and `unique_constraint(:email)`, an `Accounts.Repo` whose `get_by/2` returns nil and whose `insert/1` applies a changeset's action or returns a struct as given, `Mailer` and `Accounts.Mailer` stubs that message the driver, and a real `Accounts.TaskSupervisor`. Opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 compile with no warnings; sonnet-1 runs only from the patched copy. In all five, `import_user(%{"email" => "Ann@Example.com", "age" => "130", "role" => "member"})` with no options returns {:ok, user} with age 120 and a lowercased email and sends no mail, and `notify: true` delivers one email. Age 17 and a missing role return an error in all five. An unknown role "root" returns an error in four, but haiku-1's `String.to_existing_atom/1` accepts it and stores `:root`, an atom the VM already holds. Haiku-1's email reads 'Hi there' because `Map.get(user, :name)` is nil. The stub Repo has no database, so `unique_constraint/3` was not exercised.

Compared with the 2026-10-23 baseline per_rule, six of the 15 earlier rows change. Required keys: haiku clean to violated (haiku-1's `Map.get(user, :name)`). 'Match every expected shape...': sonnet violated to clean (both sonnets now return distinct reasons). 'Branch with function clauses...' and 'Keep functions short...': haiku clean to violated (haiku-1 misses the nesting) and sonnet violated to clean (both sonnets report it, and neither nests a block `if` in its `with`). Overlapping options: opus clean to violated (opus-1 reports `:silent` and keeps it). 'Validate input with changesets': opus and sonnet violated to clean (opus-1 builds a real `cast/3` changeset, and both sonnets insert through an assumed one instead of a `change/2` that validates nothing). The new 'Name a step...' row is clean in every tier. Rules broken per run: opus-1 5, haiku-1 14, haiku-2 10, sonnet-1 6, sonnet-2 4 of 16.
Evidence line numbers are review.md line numbers; 'input line' means code-review-input.ex.
